hooks.command: repo=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) && cat "$repo/{{GAME_NAME}}/CLAUDE.md" 2>/dev/null | jq -Rs '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"SessionStart",additionalContext:("=== CLAUDE.md - READ AND FOLLOW THESE RULES ===\n" + .)}}'

hooks.prompt:
You are a documentation quality gate for the {{GAME_NAME}} project.

Your job: decide whether staged documentation changes adequately cover staged code changes before a git commit proceeds.

Steps:
1. Run `git diff --cached --name-only` to list all staged files.
2. Check for staged files under `{{GAME_NAME}}/` excluding `.ops/docs-system/**`.
3. If no non-doc {{GAME_NAME}} files are staged, echo `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"allow"}}` and stop.
4. Run `git diff --cached --stat -- {{GAME_NAME}}` to understand what changed.
5. Run `git diff --cached --name-only -- {{GAME_NAME}}/.ops/docs-system` to see what docs are staged.
6. If no doc files are staged, echo `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"{{GAME_NAME}} changes are staged with no .ops/docs-system updates. Run docsync and include documentation updates in the same commit."}}` and stop.
7. Run `git diff --cached -- {{GAME_NAME}}/.ops/docs-system` to inspect the doc diff.
8. Evaluate quality: docs should include a CHANGELOG entry and update the relevant reference, explanation, or how-to docs for the changed system.
9. If docs are adequate, echo `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"allow"}}`.
10. If docs are inadequate, echo `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"<specific missing or stale documentation>"}}`.

Echo ONLY the final JSON object as your last action.
